text: {{CcoCampaignEventDilemma:ScriptObjectContext("land_enc_spot_battle_missions").StringValue}}A Cathayan general blocks our path and calls out a challenge, a skirmish to settle which army is the stronger. He bows to our general with cold courtesy, as if this were a lesson he means to teach.\\n\\nBehind the general, Jade Warriors are already forming ranks with halberds levelled. Their lines are straight and silent, and their officers watch our every move.\\n\\nOur own soldiers are watching to see how we answer. Do we accept?
A Test of Arms

{{CcoCampaignEventDilemma:ScriptObjectContext("land_enc_spot_battle_missions").StringValue}}A Kislevite general blocks our path and calls out a challenge, a skirmish to settle which army is the stronger. He laughs as he shouts it, his breath steaming in the cold air.\\n\\nBehind the general, boyars wrapped in bear furs are already drawing their men into line. The soldiers pass a flask down the ranks and stamp their boots, eager to get started.\\n\\nThey will think little of us if we refuse. Do we accept?
A Test of Arms

{{CcoCampaignEventDilemma:ScriptObjectContext("land_enc_spot_battle_missions").StringValue}}An Ogre general blocks our path and calls out a challenge, a skirmish to settle which army is the stronger. His voice rolls over our column like thunder.\\n\\nBehind the general, his warriors slap their gut-plates and drool at the thought of the feast to come. Some are already arguing over who gets to eat which of us.\\n\\nOgres respect strength and little else. If we refuse, they will only remember us as a meal that got away. Do we accept?
A Test of Arms

{{CcoCampaignEventDilemma:ScriptObjectContext("land_enc_spot_battle_missions").StringValue}}A Nurglite general blocks our path and calls out a challenge, a skirmish to settle which army is the stronger. He speaks warmly, like an old friend, though the stench of him turns our stomachs.\\n\\nBehind the general, his rotting ranks are already shambling into line under a cloud of buzzing flies. They do not seem to feel pain, and they do not seem to mind waiting.\\n\\nOur soldiers cover their mouths and grip their weapons. Do we accept?
A Test of Arms

{{CcoCampaignEventDilemma:ScriptObjectContext("land_enc_spot_battle_missions").StringValue}}A Tzeentchian general blocks our path and calls out a challenge, a skirmish to settle which army is the stronger. His voice seems to come from several places at once.\\n\\nBehind the general, his soldiers are forming ranks under shifting, many-coloured banners. The air around them shimmers, and our scouts swear the ranks look different each time they count them.\\n\\nHe says he sees many battles in our future. Do we accept?
A Test of Arms

{{CcoCampaignEventDilemma:ScriptObjectContext("land_enc_spot_battle_missions").StringValue}}On the road we come across a battered camp full of ragged, hostile malcontents. They are thin and hungry, and they have little left to lose.\\n\\nTheir leader gives us a mocking salute, thanking the Dragon for his love. The rest raise their weapons, some with shaking hands, ready to attack. Others only watch from the tents, waiting to see what we do.\\n\\nOur soldiers close ranks and wait for orders. What should we do?
Nascent Rebellion

{{CcoCampaignEventDilemma:ScriptObjectContext("land_enc_spot_battle_missions").StringValue}}On the road we come across a battered camp full of ragged, hostile malcontents. Their fires are small, and their furs are thin against the cold.\\n\\nTheir leader gives us a mocking salute, thanking Ursun for his love. The rest raise their weapons, some with shaking hands, ready to attack. Others only watch from the huts, waiting to see what we do.\\n\\nOur soldiers close ranks and wait for orders. What should we do?
Nascent Rebellion

{{CcoCampaignEventDilemma:ScriptObjectContext("land_enc_spot_battle_missions").StringValue}}On the road we come across a battered camp full of ragged, hostile malcontents. The cooking pits are empty, and hunger has made them bold.\\n\\nTheir leader gives us a mocking salute, thanking the Maw for its blessings. The rest raise their weapons, some with shaking hands, ready to attack. Others only watch from the shadows, waiting to see what we do.\\n\\nOur soldiers close ranks and wait for orders. What should we do?
Nascent Rebellion

{{CcoCampaignEventDilemma:ScriptObjectContext("land_enc_spot_battle_missions").StringValue}}On the road we come across a battered camp full of ragged, hostile malcontents. Strange symbols are scratched into the posts of their tents.\\n\\nTheir leader gives us a mocking salute, thanking the gods of Chaos for their power. The rest raise their weapons, some with shaking hands, ready to attack. Others only mutter prayers, waiting to see what we do.\\n\\nOur soldiers close ranks and wait for orders. What should we do?
Nascent Rebellion

{{CcoCampaignEventDilemma:ScriptObjectContext("land_enc_spot_battle_missions").StringValue}}A faint smell of gunpowder drifts across the empty road, and the soldiers feel they are being watched. The farms on either side stand dark, with no smoke from their chimneys.\\n\\nAs the vanguard advances, a birdcall sounds from the hedges, and another answers it. Our scouts say no bird sings like that. Someone out there is passing signals.\\n\\nThe officers keep their hands near their weapons. Should we continue down this path?
Bandits!

{{CcoCampaignEventDilemma:ScriptObjectContext("land_enc_spot_battle_missions").StringValue}}The army pushes through a thick, damp forest where little light reaches the ground. Moss covers every stone, and the path keeps vanishing under the roots.\\n\\nEvery snapping twig sounds like a footstep, and the trees seem to shift when no one is looking. The vanguard reports voices among the branches and advises us to prepare for an ambush.\\n\\nThe men are uneasy and keep close together. Should we continue down this path?
Bandits!

{{CcoCampaignEventDilemma:ScriptObjectContext("land_enc_spot_battle_missions").StringValue}}Hoofbeats and howling circle the long line of the army on every side. Our outriders catch only glimpses of furs and painted shields between the hills.\\n\\nCrazed screams and curses in a crude, guttural tongue ring out, but no one shows themselves. They seem to be followers of the Dark Gods, and they want a toll before they let us through.\\n\\nOur soldiers keep their shields up and watch the hills. What should we do?
Bandits!

{{CcoCampaignEventDilemma:ScriptObjectContext("land_enc_spot_battle_missions").StringValue}}The cackle of hobgoblins fills the night air, coming from every shadow around us. Our sentries double the watch and keep the fires burning high.\\n\\nWe see the slavers circling our encampment, testing whether it can be easily assaulted. Chains rattle somewhere in the dark, and the wolves they ride snarl at our horses.\\n\\nThey seem sloppy and overconfident. Our officers think we could catch them off guard. What should we do?
Bandits!

{{CcoCampaignEventDilemma:ScriptObjectContext("land_enc_spot_battle_missions").StringValue}}Our advance party reports a large band of invaders in the distance. They are pushing into lands we claim, looting small towns and carting off their stores. Corpses riddled with arrows lie everywhere.\\n\\nSome survivors, deliberately left alive, tell our general it was "for the good of all". They say the elves did not even look at them as they marched past.\\n\\nThe invaders mean to settle this land, or strip it bare if they cannot hold it.
Raid!

{{CcoCampaignEventDilemma:ScriptObjectContext("land_enc_spot_battle_missions").StringValue}}Our advance party reports a large band of invaders in the distance. They are pushing into lands we claim, looting small towns and carting off their stores. Half-eaten corpses and trampled houses are everywhere.\\n\\nSome survivors, deliberately left alive, babble to our general about "giant lizards" and lizardmen. They are still shaking as they speak.\\n\\nThe invaders mean to settle this land, or strip it bare if they cannot hold it.
Raid!

{{CcoCampaignEventDilemma:ScriptObjectContext("land_enc_spot_battle_missions").StringValue}}Our advance party reports a large band of invaders in the distance. They are pushing into lands we claim, looting small towns and carting off their stores.\\n\\nNo corpses are seen anywhere. Most of the towns seem abandoned, with traces of sea water where there should be none. The use of magic here is clearly felt.\\n\\nThe invaders mean to settle this land, or strip it bare if they cannot hold it.
Raid!

{{CcoCampaignEventDilemma:ScriptObjectContext("land_enc_spot_battle_missions").StringValue}}The forest glows under the light of Morrslieb as the army passes through. The night is full of sounds that should not be there, and guttural grunts carry from the edges of the column.\\n\\nA huge beast crashes into the outer column before our soldiers drive it back. It leaves broken men and a smell of wet fur behind it. More shapes are moving in the trees.\\n\\nThe soldiers look to their general for orders. What should we do?
Possible Ambush?

{{CcoCampaignEventDilemma:ScriptObjectContext("land_enc_spot_battle_missions").StringValue}}The road winds through a pass between the mountains. Small caves surround the path and the silence is heavy. A foul smell drifts up from the dark.\\n\\nThe outer columns warn of red eyes in the dark, and the chattering is too loud to come from ordinary rats. Something is scraping and digging under the rocks.\\n\\nThe soldiers of the vanguard advise attacking the caves before they attack us! What should we do?
Possible Ambush?

{{CcoCampaignEventDilemma:ScriptObjectContext("land_enc_spot_battle_missions").StringValue}}A great greenskin horde gathers on the hilltop, beating crude drums and bellowing insults down the slope. Their banners are made of bones and stolen cloth.\\n\\nThey are waiting for our column to halt so they can charge. The biggest of them push to the front, shoving smaller goblins out of the way to get the first swing.\\n\\nIt will be a hard fight, but a horde this size will not go away on its own. Shall we try our luck?
An Epic Battle!

{{CcoCampaignEventDilemma:ScriptObjectContext("land_enc_spot_battle_missions").StringValue}}A large army of dark elf slavers has made camp in a remote corner of this province, empty cages stacked on its wagons. Their sentries are few, and their fires burn low.\\n\\nThey clearly mean to raid our settlements for slaves. If they march, the villages nearby will be emptied before word reaches us.\\n\\nThe rough ground has hidden our approach, and they have not seen us yet. Should we try to intercept them?
An Epic Battle!

{{CcoCampaignEventDilemma:ScriptObjectContext("land_enc_spot_battle_missions").StringValue}}Locals tell of a necromancer hiding in a remote graveyard, where the earth is turned over fresh every night. No one dares go near it after dark.\\n\\nHe is raising an army to march on our lands, and it grows with every grave he empties. The villagers have started burning their dead rather than burying them.\\n\\nThe longer we wait, the larger his army becomes. Should we attack him before he gets out of control?
An Epic Battle!

{{CcoCampaignEventDilemma:ScriptObjectContext("land_enc_spot_battle_missions").StringValue}}Under the green light of Morrslieb, our advance party sees a strange sight. Skeletons in gold and fine linen, marching beside great constructs that move as if alive, are chasing a long band of Norscan marauders.\\n\\nThe dead march in perfect step and make no sound. The marauders run from them in fear.\\n\\nWhen they spot us, a large contingent breaks off and turns our way, ready in case we think of interfering.
An Epic Battle!

{{CcoCampaignEventDilemma:ScriptObjectContext("land_enc_spot_battle_missions").StringValue}}A huge band of Slayers stands before us, crests of orange hair bristling, and Gotrek and Felix march at its head. They are bare-chested, covered in tattoos, and they carry axes as big as a man.\\n\\nThey seem to have been sent to destroy us, and they keep chasing us on their short legs no matter how much ground we put between us.\\n\\nThey will not stop until they get their fight. Why are we in the dwarfs' Book of Grudges?
An Epic Battle!
A Gift From Chaos

{{CcoCampaignEventDilemma:ScriptObjectContext("land_enc_spot_battle_missions").StringValue}}"SKARBRAND HATES YOU!" the Bloodthirster bellows. The ground shakes as he strides closer, his axes dragging furrows through the earth.\\n\\n"YOUR SKULL BELONGS AT THE FOOT OF THE THRONE! PREPARE TO DIE!"\\n\\nThe gaze of the Blood God falls on us, and the ranks grip their weapons tighter. The air smells of blood and hot iron. No one here means to run from him.
A Gift From Chaos

{{CcoCampaignEventDilemma:ScriptObjectContext("land_enc_spot_battle_missions").StringValue}}Khorne's consort towers over us like a fallen angel, wings spread wide.\\n\\n"Khorne calls you to serve his glory! I will be the one to test you! I will be the one to decide if you are worthy to worship our lord! Die and let me decorate his throne with your skull!"\\n\\nThe Blood God is watching. Our warriors hold their ground, eager to prove they are worth his notice.
A Gift From Chaos

{{CcoCampaignEventDilemma:ScriptObjectContext("land_enc_spot_battle_missions").StringValue}}Our lord dreams of a fiery-eyed warrior who points the way to a hidden clearing near the camp. On waking, a strange fury takes hold, and the army marches to the place from the dream. A greater daemon and its warband are there, and they did not expect us. "Who dares defy the will of the Blood God? Prepare to die." The daemonic army readies to attack. The fury from the dream has not faded. The army wants this fight, and the Blood God is watching.
A Gift From Chaos

{{CcoCampaignEventDilemma:ScriptObjectContext("land_enc_spot_battle_missions").StringValue}}A huge, swift daemon approaches, and we know him from the stories. Azazel looks at us almost fondly. "Little one, there is something strange about this sword. I think the Dark Prince blessed it once, but now it reeks of blood and rage, and it makes the dead come after me. Don't get me wrong, it's a lot of fun. But if we fight here, I think I can be rid of it. What do you say? It's a fun idea, isn't it?" He waits, hopeful. The blade has gone over to the Blood God, and so has the warband around it. Somewhere beyond the veil, the Blood God is watching. Our warriors are hungry for this fight.
A Gift From Chaos

{{CcoCampaignEventDilemma:ScriptObjectContext("land_enc_spot_battle_missions").StringValue}}We come upon a lavish, openly debauched camp that looks more like a carnival than a war camp. Its general is Sigvald the Magnificent, beautiful as a painted saint, and he looks us over with open disgust. "My god sometimes surprises me when he presents me with horrible, unpresentable things like you." He waves a scornful hand but keeps talking. "He sent me to give you a gift so that you would consider joining us. But seeing you here, so pathetic and weak, I have decided to keep it. You are clearly undeserving of his favour." The Dark Prince's gaze rests on us, sweet as poison. Our greed will not let him keep what was meant for us. Embrace the temptation!
A Gift From Chaos

{{CcoCampaignEventDilemma:ScriptObjectContext("land_enc_spot_battle_missions").StringValue}}A strange, magnificent castle stands where none stood before, plainly a work of Chaos, and we feel compelled to enter. Wine runs from the fountains and the halls ring with revelry. N'Kari, the Keeper of Secrets, welcomes us. "Nice to have you here. Do you feel her gaze? She makes me feel... wild. She wants to see you and me fight. I promise if you win I'll make it count for you." The daemon licks his lips with a long, lascivious tongue. "And if you lose, well, we'll still have fun... as much as possible." He laughs. The Dark Prince's gaze rests on us, sweet as poison. The hunger in our heart urges us to take his challenge. Embrace the temptation!
A Gift From Chaos

{{CcoCampaignEventDilemma:ScriptObjectContext("land_enc_spot_battle_missions").StringValue}}Deep in the night our lookouts start screaming, and some of them die before the camp is roused. An emissary walks out of the dark, a stunningly beautiful dark elf. "The Dark Prince wants me to present you with a gift. It seems that he has chosen you as his protégé. But I can always get a better deal if I kidnap you instead of giving you his gift." She weighs us with a calculating gaze. "I'll give you a chance to disappear. He's never liked cowards, so if he sees you running away I can just take his gift. Make a decision or die." The Dark Prince's gaze rests on us, sweet as poison. Our greed will not let her walk off with what is ours. Embrace the temptation!

This smithy is held by [[col:red]]{{CcoCampaignEventDilemma:ScriptObjectContext("land_enc_point_owner").StringValue}}[[/col]], and its master has hired blades to guard the forge. We can storm it and take it for ourselves, opening its forge to our generals and heroes, though a grander forge keeps tougher guards.\\n\\nWin the battle and the smithy is ours. Lose, and it stays under their control.\\n\\n{{CcoCampaignEventDilemma:ScriptObjectContext("land_enc_point_relations").StringValue}}
Seizing the Smithy

An enemy army marches on the smithy. Our scouts saw its banners on the road, and it will be here before nightfall.\\n\\nThe blacksmiths take up weapons from their own racks, and the guard detachment forms up at the forge door. They are brave, but they are few, and the enemy is many.\\n\\nIf we do not stand with them, the smithy falls into enemy hands, and its forges will start making weapons for our enemies.
Defending the Smithy

The master blacksmith looks at us anxiously and asks us to choose one of his works. The smithy is small, and its tools are old and worn.\\n\\nThe quality is clearly poor, but it will still serve our army. A blade that is ugly can still cut.\\n\\nOr we could give him the gold to expand the smithy, so that it pays its taxes faster and turns out better equipment on our next visit.
The Master Blacksmith's Offer

The master blacksmith looks at us seriously and asks us to choose one of his works. The smithy has grown since our last visit, and the forge burns hotter.\\n\\nThe quality is clearly good, and it will serve our army well.\\n\\nOr we could give him the gold to expand the smithy, so that it pays its taxes faster and turns out better equipment on our next visit.
The Master Blacksmith's Trust

The master blacksmith smiles and asks us to choose one of his masterpieces. The smithy is now one of the finest in the land, and its forge never goes cold.\\n\\nThe quality is clearly excellent, and it will serve our army well. Each piece carries his mark, and he is proud to see it go with us.\\n\\nOur soldiers crowd around the racks to look. Few armies are offered work like this.
The Master Blacksmith's Gift
A Test of Arms

{{CcoCampaignEventDilemma:ScriptObjectContext("land_enc_spot_battle_missions").StringValue}}A rival general blocks the road with a modest force and calls out a challenge. His soldiers stand ready, shields up and weapons drawn.\\n\\nThey want to see whether our army is worth fearing. Word of the result will travel fast, whichever way it goes.\\n\\nOur own soldiers are watching to see how we answer. Do we accept?
Nascent Rebellion

{{CcoCampaignEventDilemma:ScriptObjectContext("land_enc_spot_battle_missions").StringValue}}We come across a battered camp full of armed malcontents who clearly do not welcome our presence. The camp is dirty and crowded, and the people in it look hungry.\\n\\nTheir leaders shout for blood, and the mob raises its weapons. Some hang back, unsure, but most are ready to fight.\\n\\nOur soldiers close ranks and wait for orders. What should we do?
Bandits!

{{CcoCampaignEventDilemma:ScriptObjectContext("land_enc_spot_battle_missions").StringValue}}The road ahead is too quiet. No travellers pass us, and the birds have gone silent.\\n\\nFresh hoofprints cross it in every direction, and the scouts swear riders are shadowing the column from the tree line. Whoever they are, they know this ground better than we do.\\n\\nThe soldiers close ranks and watch the trees. Should we continue down this path?
Possible Ambush?

{{CcoCampaignEventDilemma:ScriptObjectContext("land_enc_spot_battle_missions").StringValue}}The column stretches thin through broken ground. The path is narrow, and the wagons slow everyone down.\\n\\nToo many birds take flight at once, and the rearguard reports shapes moving along the ridges. Whoever is up there is keeping pace with us.\\n\\nThe soldiers look to their general. What should we do?
Raid!

{{CcoCampaignEventDilemma:ScriptObjectContext("land_enc_spot_battle_missions").StringValue}}Our advance party reports a large foreign force in the distance, looting small towns and carting off everything of value. Smoke rises from the farms they have already passed.\\n\\nThe survivors say the invaders mean to take this land or strip it bare. They have lost their homes and ask us to drive the invaders out.\\n\\nWhat should we do?
An Epic Battle!

{{CcoCampaignEventDilemma:ScriptObjectContext("land_enc_spot_battle_missions").StringValue}}A great army waits in battle lines on the far side of the field, banners raised and war drums pounding. The ground between us is open and flat.\\n\\nIts general has chosen this ground and expects us to answer. His soldiers are rested and ready, and there are more of them than our scouts first thought.\\n\\nIt will be a hard fight. Shall we try our luck?
The Master Blacksmith's Forge

The master blacksmith shows us what the forge has on hand. The racks are full, and the anvils ring with work.\\n\\nWe may take one piece freely while the forge is ready, commission a masterwork for gold, or pay to improve the forge so its work grows finer.\\n\\nThe smith waits for our choice, wiping his hands on his apron.
The Master Blacksmith's Forge

The master blacksmith wipes the soot from his hands: "Not much on the racks yet, but every piece is honest work."\\n\\nThis forge belongs to the [[col:yellow]]Smiths' Association[[/col]], which honours its patrons at every smithy.\\n\\n[[col:yellow]]Forge level 1 of 3[[/col]]\\n- Free pieces: [[col:yellow]]common or uncommon[[/col]], one per visit\\n- Ready again: [[col:yellow]]5 turns[[/col]] longer than the Smithy cooldown after a free piece (10 turns by default)\\n- Commission: one rare masterwork for [[col:yellow]]5000[[/col]] gold\\n- Tribute: one item every [[col:yellow]]15 turns[[/col]]\\n- Improve to level 2: [[col:yellow]]10000[[/col]] gold
The Master Blacksmith's Forge

The master blacksmith nods towards the racks: "Good steel, all of it. The Association stamped every piece itself."\\n\\nThis forge belongs to the [[col:yellow]]Smiths' Association[[/col]], which honours its patrons at every smithy.\\n\\n[[col:yellow]]Forge level 2 of 3[[/col]]\\n- Free pieces: [[col:yellow]]uncommon or rare[[/col]], one per visit\\n- Ready again: [[col:yellow]]2 turns[[/col]] longer than the Smithy cooldown after a free piece (7 turns by default)\\n- Commission: one rare masterwork for [[col:yellow]]10000[[/col]] gold\\n- Tribute: one item every [[col:yellow]]10 turns[[/col]]\\n- Improve to level 3: [[col:yellow]]20000[[/col]] gold
The Master Blacksmith's Forge

The master blacksmith spreads his arms over the racks: "The finest work in the Association. Take your pick."\\n\\nThis forge belongs to the [[col:yellow]]Smiths' Association[[/col]], which honours its patrons at every smithy.\\n\\n[[col:yellow]]Forge level 3 of 3[[/col]]\\n- Free pieces: [[col:yellow]]rare[[/col]], one per visit\\n- Ready again: after the [[col:yellow]]Smithy cooldown[[/col]] once a free piece is taken (5 turns by default)\\n- Commission: two rare masterworks for [[col:yellow]]15000[[/col]] gold\\n- Tribute: one item every [[col:yellow]]5 turns[[/col]]\\n- Unique commission: one unique piece for [[col:yellow]]20000[[/col]] gold
The Ancient Tower

An ancient tower rises before us, its gates held by a hostile warband. Five floors lead up to the Master of the Tower, and every floor we take adds to the haul.\\n\\n[[col:yellow]]Floors[[/col]]\\n- Floor 1: easy\\n- Floors 2 to 4: medium\\n- Floor 5: the Master of the Tower, hard\\n\\nAfter each victory we may climb higher or leave with the haul. Our losses carry over from floor to floor. [[col:red]]Losing any floor forfeits the whole haul.[[/col]]\\n\\n[[col:yellow]]Between floors[[/col]]\\nAfter each victory the tower offers deals for the climb ahead: healing, buffs, sabotage, gambles and more. [[col:yellow]]Missions[[/col]] set a goal for the next battle and pay only if we fight that battle ourselves. [[col:red]]An auto-resolved battle does not count.[[/col]]
The Master Has Fallen

{{CcoCampaignEventDilemma:ScriptObjectContext("land_enc_tower_result_floor_5").StringValue}}The Master of the Tower lies dead at our feet, and every floor is ours. Its vaults stand open. The bodies of its guards lie behind us, and the stairs are quiet at last. Our soldiers go room by room, counting what the Master kept.\\n\\n[[col:yellow]]The climb[[/col]]\\n{{CcoCampaignEventDilemma:ScriptObjectContext("land_enc_tower_climb_floor_5").StringValue}}\\n\\n[[col:yellow]]The whole haul is ours to claim.[[/col]]
Tower Floor 1 Cleared

{{CcoCampaignEventDilemma:ScriptObjectContext("land_enc_tower_result_floor_1").StringValue}}The floor is ours, and the way up lies open. Our army has had no time to recover.\\n\\n[[col:yellow]]The climb[[/col]]\\n{{CcoCampaignEventDilemma:ScriptObjectContext("land_enc_tower_climb_floor_1").StringValue}}\\n\\n[[col:yellow]]Floor 2 adds to the haul[[/col]]\\n- 2000 gold, up to 3000 for a clean win\\n- 2 uncommon or rare items\\n\\nClimb higher for a richer haul, or leave now and keep what we have. [[col:red]]Losing the next floor forfeits the whole haul.[[/col]]\\n\\n[[col:yellow]]Missions[[/col]] set a goal for the next battle and pay only if we fight that battle ourselves. [[col:red]]An auto-resolved battle does not count.[[/col]]
An Ally Beset

{{CcoCampaignEventDilemma:ScriptObjectContext("land_enc_spot_battle_missions").StringValue}}Smoke rises beyond the next ridge, where an allied army stands surrounded. We can hear the clash of steel and the shouts of their officers from here.\\n\\nTheir lines are bending, and the enemy brought far more warriors than it needs. If we march now, we can fight at their side and turn the day.\\n\\nWin, and their kin across these lands will remember who came to help.
Turn the Tables

{{CcoCampaignEventDilemma:ScriptObjectContext("land_enc_spot_battle_missions").StringValue}}The scouts of our allied escort come back at a run. An enemy war party lies hidden along the road ahead, waiting for us to walk into its trap.\\n\\nIt does not know it has been seen. If we strike first, together, we can catch it in the open before it is ready. Our soldiers check their weapons and wait for the word.\\n\\nWin, and the escort's kin will hear of it.
Relief Column

{{CcoCampaignEventDilemma:ScriptObjectContext("land_enc_spot_battle_missions").StringValue}}A messenger reaches us half dead. An allied army is cut off, and the enemy is closing in for the kill. His horse collapses as he gives his report.\\n\\nThey will not hold for long. If we march hard, we can reach them before their line breaks. Every hour we wait costs them more men.\\n\\nSome of those we save may choose to fight under our banner.
The Tavern

{{CcoCampaignEventDilemma:ScriptObjectContext("land_enc_tavern_scene").StringValue}}\\n\\n{{CcoCampaignEventDilemma:ScriptObjectContext("land_enc_tavern_greeting").StringValue}}\\n\\n[[col:yellow]]Tavern level 1 of 3[[/col]]\\n- Run by the Tavern Keepers' Guild: hold 1 of its contracts at a time, from any of its Taverns.\\n- Owned by [[col:yellow]]{{CcoCampaignEventDilemma:ScriptObjectContext("land_enc_point_owner").StringValue}}[[/col]]. Only the owner can improve it.
The Tavern

{{CcoCampaignEventDilemma:ScriptObjectContext("land_enc_tavern_scene").StringValue}}\\n\\n{{CcoCampaignEventDilemma:ScriptObjectContext("land_enc_tavern_greeting").StringValue}}\\n\\n[[col:yellow]]Tavern level 2 of 3[[/col]]\\n- Run by the Tavern Keepers' Guild: hold 1 of its contracts at a time, from any of its Taverns.\\n- Owned by [[col:yellow]]{{CcoCampaignEventDilemma:ScriptObjectContext("land_enc_point_owner").StringValue}}[[/col]]. Only the owner can improve it.
The Tavern

{{CcoCampaignEventDilemma:ScriptObjectContext("land_enc_tavern_scene").StringValue}}\\n\\n{{CcoCampaignEventDilemma:ScriptObjectContext("land_enc_tavern_greeting").StringValue}}\\n\\n[[col:yellow]]Tavern level 3 of 3[[/col]]\\n- Run by the Tavern Keepers' Guild: hold 1 of its contracts at a time, from any of its Taverns.\\n- Owned by [[col:yellow]]{{CcoCampaignEventDilemma:ScriptObjectContext("land_enc_point_owner").StringValue}}[[/col]]. Only the owner can improve it.
Seizing the Tavern

This tavern is held by [[col:red]]{{CcoCampaignEventDilemma:ScriptObjectContext("land_enc_point_owner").StringValue}}[[/col]], and its keeper has hired blades to guard the premises. We can storm it and take it for ourselves, though a grander tavern keeps tougher guards.\\n\\nWin the battle and the tavern is ours. Lose, and it stays in their hands.\\n\\n{{CcoCampaignEventDilemma:ScriptObjectContext("land_enc_point_relations").StringValue}}
Defending the Tavern

An enemy army marches on the tavern. Our scouts saw its banners on the road, and it will be here before nightfall.\\n\\nThe keeper bars the door, and the guards he hired form up in the yard with their weapons drawn. They are paid to fight, but not to die, and they will not hold alone.\\n\\nIf we do not stand with them, the tavern falls into enemy hands.
The Mercenary Hall

Sellswords of every stripe drink and dice in the back hall, waiting for a lord with gold. The companies here are for hire to every visitor, for a price, and new ones arrive every 5 turns.\\n\\nThe broker looks up from his ledger: "Gold first, then take your pick. Two companies at most. I can't have you emptying the place."\\n\\n[[col:yellow]]By Tavern level:[[/col]]\\n- Level 1: 3 companies of tier 1 or 2, and 1 of our own kind.\\n- Level 2: 4 companies up to tier 3, 1 famous regiment, 1 of our own kind and a rank 5 hero.\\n- Level 3: 5 companies up to tier 4, 1 or 2 famous regiments, 2 of our own kind and a rank 10 hero.\\n\\n[[col:yellow]]Hire up to 2, after which the hall will not deal with us for 5 turns, or go back to the common room.[[/col]]
The Contract Board

Notices crowd the board by the door, each stamped with the seal of the Tavern Keepers' Guild: bounties on lords who have made enemies of the Guild, and purses for anyone who will thin out a foe troubling its roads. Each contract asks a deposit, returned with the reward when the work is done. Fail one or drop it, and the deposit is lost. Every Tavern of the Guild then charges us a quarter more for 10 turns.\\n\\nA Guild clerk taps the board with an inky finger: "Read them carefully. The Guild does not forget a broken contract."\\n\\n[[col:yellow]]By Tavern level:[[/col]]\\n- Level 1: easy contracts for a 1000 gold deposit, paying 1500 to 2000 gold and an uncommon item. Culls ask for 2 armies.\\n- Level 2: medium contracts for a 2000 gold deposit, paying 3000 to 3500 gold and a rare item. Culls ask for 3 armies.\\n- Level 3: hard contracts for a 3000 gold deposit, paying 4500 to 5000 gold and a rare item. Culls ask for 4 armies, and a three-step quest ends with a legendary item.\\n\\n[[col:yellow]]We can hold 1 contract at a time, from any Tavern. Drop it from the missions panel to take another.[[/col]]
Hidden Tomb

A forgotten tomb lies half-buried in the hillside, its door split by roots and time. Our scouts found it by chance.\\n\\nThe wards carved into the stone are old, but not all of them have failed. The air at the threshold is colder than it should be.\\n\\nWhatever was laid to rest here was buried with care, and with wealth. Something inside still remembers how to bite.\\n\\n[[col:yellow]]Choose one, or walk away.[[/col]]
Abandoned Camp

Cold fires and empty tents stand in a sheltered hollow. The ashes are grey and long dead, and the canvas flaps loose in the wind.\\n\\nWhoever camped here left in a hurry. Bedrolls lie where they were dropped, and a cookpot still hangs over the fire pit. There are no bodies and no sign of a fight, only boot prints leading away in every direction.\\n\\nThey left their stores and a fair share of loot behind, and no one has come back for it.\\n\\n[[col:yellow]]Choose one, or walk away.[[/col]]
Buried Relics

Bones of something enormous jut from the churned earth. Our soldiers give them a wide berth.\\n\\nAmong them lie older things, weapons and charms buried long before the beast ever died here. Rusted blades and cracked amulets turn up wherever the ground is torn.\\n\\nWhoever buried them meant them to stay hidden. The beast's death has brought them back to the surface.\\n\\n[[col:yellow]]Choose one, or walk away.[[/col]]
Hidden Temple

A temple rises from the wilds, its walls choked with vines but its altar swept clean, as if someone still tends it. No path leads here.\\n\\nIts keepers left long ago. The carvings on the pillars are worn smooth and the roof has fallen in places, letting the rain onto the old stones.\\n\\nYet offerings laid here are still answered. The men speak quietly inside, and few of them care to stay after dark.\\n\\n[[col:yellow]]Choose one, or walk away.[[/col]]
Caravan Remnants

A half-sacked caravan lies across the road, its wagons overturned and its goods scattered in the mud. The drivers are dead or fled.\\n\\nThe raiders were in a hurry. They cut open sacks and smashed crates, took what they could carry and rode off before anyone could stop them.\\n\\nThey missed more than they took. There is still plenty here for an army willing to dig through the wreckage.\\n\\n[[col:yellow]]Choose one, or walk away.[[/col]]
A Voice in the Dream

Our lord wakes from a dream more vivid than any waking hour. The dream will not fade.\\n\\nA voice spoke in it, offering strength for the trials ahead. It knew our lord's name, our road and the battles still to come.\\n\\nThe voice offered many gifts, but not all of them are free. Some of its gifts come with a price, and it did not say what that price would be.\\n\\n[[col:yellow]]Choose one, or walk away.[[/col]]
The Explorers

A band of weathered explorers shares our fire for the night. They know the land well.\\n\\nThey trade maps and tales of the road ahead, of passes, rivers and the dangers waiting beyond them. Some of what they say is surely boasting, but much of it rings true.\\n\\nThey ask only for safe passage in return. Few travellers are so easy to deal with in these lands.\\n\\n[[col:yellow]]Choose one, or walk away.[[/col]]
Legendary Bard

A famous bard sits in chains in a bandit camp we have just put to flight. The bandits kept them to sing at their fires.\\n\\nThe bard's name is known in courts and taverns far from here. Their songs travel faster than any army.\\n\\nFreed, they promise to sing of our deeds in every hall and war camp across the land. A song like that could carry our name a long way.\\n\\n[[col:yellow]]Choose one, or walk away.[[/col]]
Ruined Shrine

A burnt-out shrine stands by the road, its idols blackened and cracked. The roof has long since fallen in.\\n\\nNo one knows who burned it. Still, small offerings lie fresh at the foot of the broken altar.\\n\\nOfferings left here may be answered with a blessing, or with something far less kind. Our soldiers keep their distance and watch the shadows.\\n\\n[[col:yellow]]Choose one, or walk away.[[/col]]
Smugglers' Cache

Crates and barrels lie hidden under a false floor in a ruined barn. Our scouts found them by chance.\\n\\nTheir owners watch us from the treeline. They are armed, but they know better than to start a fight with an army.\\n\\nThey deal in goods and secrets, and they are open to offers. Not everything they sell is honest, but all of it is useful.\\n\\n[[col:yellow]]Choose one, or walk away.[[/col]]
Beast Lair

Something big lives in this cave. Fresh bones litter the entrance, some of them still red.\\n\\nThe stench carries on the wind for a mile. Our horses will not go near it, and the men grow quiet as we draw close.\\n\\nA lair like this often holds the remains of those who came before us, along with whatever they carried.\\n\\n[[col:yellow]]Choose one, or walk away.[[/col]]
Old Battlefield

Crows wheel over an old battlefield where two armies broke each other long ago. No one came back to bury the dead.\\n\\nWrecked war machines and unburied bones still lie half sunk in the mud. Rusted armour and broken banners cover the ground.\\n\\nThe dead have no more use for what they left behind. Our soldiers pick their way through the field with care.\\n\\n[[col:yellow]]Choose one, or walk away.[[/col]]
Witch's Hut

A crooked hut squats in the marsh, thick with smoke and stranger smells. Charms of bone and feather hang from the eaves.\\n\\nThe witch who lives here deals in pacts and curses. She knew we were coming before our scouts reached her door, and she has been waiting for us.\\n\\nShe will offer her help, but every one of her bargains has a price. Few who deal with her walk away unchanged.\\n\\n[[col:yellow]]Choose one, or walk away.[[/col]]
Collapsed Mine

A collapsed mine yawns in the hillside, its lower galleries half-flooded. Broken carts and rotten timbers block the main shaft.\\n\\nThe deeper tunnels are still rich. Veins of ore glint in the torchlight, and the old miners left tools and stores behind when they fled.\\n\\nThe tunnels are still deadly to anyone who lingers. The roof groans and shifts, and the water rises a little more each day.\\n\\n[[col:yellow]]Choose one, or walk away.[[/col]]
Merchant's Wagon

A travelling merchant has lost the road and most of their escort. Their wagon creaks into our camp on a cracked wheel.\\n\\nThe merchant is shaken, but they know their trade. The wagon is packed with goods from far away, some useful, some strange, and all of it for sale.\\n\\nFar from any market and glad of any customer, they throw open their wagon to us. Prices are fair, for once.\\n\\n[[col:yellow]]Choose one, or walk away.[[/col]]
Sunken Library

A library has sunk into the marsh, its shelves rotting in black water. Only the upper floors still stand above the water.\\n\\nMost of the books are lost to mould and mud. Some scrolls survive, sealed in wax and lead, holding the secrets of other realms.\\n\\nReaching them means wading into cold, deep water. Our scouts say something moves beneath the surface.\\n\\n[[col:yellow]]Choose one, or walk away.[[/col]]
Spoils of War

The field is ours. Enemy dead lie in heaps, and the wounded are being gathered from the mud. The crows are already circling.\\n\\nTheir baggage stands abandoned where they broke and ran. Wagons, weapons and supplies lie scattered across the ground, and our soldiers are already picking through them.\\n\\nBefore we march on, there is more to take from this victory. The men have earned it, and the enemy has no further use for it.\\n\\n[[col:yellow]]Choose one, or walk away.[[/col]]
The Bar

The keeper leans on the bar beside barrels for every taste. Over at the tables, strangers are rolling dice, and a hulking champion waits for anyone brave enough to lock arms with them.\\n\\nThe barkeep turns to us: "What'll it be?"\\n\\n[[col:yellow]]By Tavern level:[[/col]]\\n- Level 1: the house brews (Fighting Spirits gives +5), a feast heals half of each unit's losses, rumours cover the 3 nearest regions, and beating the champion is worth 500 experience.\\n- Level 2: stronger brews (+10), a feast heals three quarters of the losses, rumours cover 5 regions, and the champion is worth 750 experience.\\n- Level 3: the strongest brews (+15), a feast heals every loss, rumours cover 7 regions, and the champion is worth 1000 experience.\\n\\n[[col:yellow]]Choose one, or go back to the common room.[[/col]]
Too Many Blessings

[[col:yellow]]{{CcoCampaignEventDilemma:ScriptObjectContext("land_enc_boon_lord").StringValue}}[[/col]] can carry no more boons. To take the new one, another must be given up.\\n\\n[[col:yellow]]What giving one up costs[[/col]]\\n- A boon given up is gone for good, with every level it has gained.\\n- The new boon is on the last choice. Refusing it keeps every boon as it is.\\n\\n[[col:yellow]]How boons grow[[/col]]\\n- A boon grows one level for every 5 battles this lord wins, up to level 5.\\n- Lost battles do not count, but they never take a level away.
Spoils of the Champion

The champion has fallen, and something of its power can be claimed. Choose one boon for [[col:yellow]]{{CcoCampaignEventDilemma:ScriptObjectContext("land_enc_boon_lord").StringValue}}[[/col]].\\n\\n[[col:yellow]]The boons on offer[[/col]]\\n- Each starts at level 1. The ones not chosen are lost.\\n- If [[col:yellow]]{{CcoCampaignEventDilemma:ScriptObjectContext("land_enc_boon_lord").StringValue}}[[/col]] has no free slot, another boon must be given up to take it.\\n\\n[[col:yellow]]How boons grow[[/col]]\\n- A boon grows one level for every 5 battles this lord wins, up to level 5.\\n- Lost battles do not count, but they never take a level away.
Temper and Break

{{CcoCampaignEventDilemma:ScriptObjectContext("land_enc_boon_service_result").StringValue}}The master smith clears the anvil for [[col:yellow]]{{CcoCampaignEventDilemma:ScriptObjectContext("land_enc_boon_lord").StringValue}}[[/col]]. Steel can be tempered here, and old curses beaten out of it.\\n\\n[[col:yellow]]What the forge offers[[/col]]\\n- Temper a boon: it rises one level. The price grows with the level it reaches.\\n- Break a curse: it is gone for good. The price grows with the curse's level.\\n- Rust for Iron: a pact that hardens the army's hide and rusts its blades.\\n\\n[[col:yellow]]Prices[[/col]]\\n- As the owner, we pay 25% less than the smith's usual rates. The room never cools down.
The Hedge-Witch

{{CcoCampaignEventDilemma:ScriptObjectContext("land_enc_boon_service_result").StringValue}}Behind a curtain of dried herbs, the hedge-witch looks [[col:yellow]]{{CcoCampaignEventDilemma:ScriptObjectContext("land_enc_boon_lord").StringValue}}[[/col]] over and smiles. Each service waits 5 turns after use, and the owner pays 25% less.\\n\\n[[col:yellow]]Boons[[/col]]\\n- Feed: 2 more won battles toward its next level.\\n- Reweave: 50% it rises a level, or it becomes another boon.\\n\\n[[col:yellow]]Curses[[/col]]\\n- Cleanse: it lifts for good.\\n- Gamble: cheaper, but lifts 50% of the time, or becomes another curse.\\n- Blood rite: lifts for no gold, but the army bleeds 5% per level.
